annotations.text:
Dial D · axis: progress line (no ring).
Why: the 64px ring reports one number (1 of 18) and nothing about structure; the 2px track with eighteen numbered nodes shows position and the four part groups at once, and the active node in clay #c8472f with a white numeral is the strongest position marker of the three. Measured at 1440: card 196 × 635px, rows 26px minimum at .74rem, tag pill on every row, numerals #6b625a on cream nodes.
Trade-off: 41px taller than A (594px) because the three part labels each take a line and two of them wrap in the 148px label column, and a track implies a reading order the homepage does not have; buyers land on Available or Pricing and skip the rest.

(Recommended) Dial E · axis: two columns.
Why: measured at 1440 the card is 392 × 337px, 57% of A (594px), and it is the only one of the three that fits under the 772px sticky cap on a 768px-tall laptop (640px usable under a 96px header plus 16px offset), where A at 594px and D at 635px scroll inside the card. Nothing was shrunk to get there: rows stay 27px at .74rem, the tag pill shows on all eighteen, part boundaries are 1px hairlines above 04, 07 and 11, and a 2px progress bar replaces the ring. The body column keeps 680px on the 1140 frame, still wider than the 66ch paragraph max-width, so no reading width is lost.
Trade-off: the card is twice the shipped .tdial width (392 against 196), so the grid template on the live pages changes, and eighteen clay tag pills now sit in a denser block than in A.

Dial F · axis: collapsed parts.
Why: the homepage's four parts already name the reading structure; collapsing the three inactive parts to a header with a real count chip (3, 4 and 8 sections) keeps the ring and cuts the card to 196 × 440px at 1440, 154px shorter than A (594px), while the counts still add to 18 without opening anything.
Trade-off: 15 of the 18 sections are behind a click, and the open/closed state needs a script the shipped .tdial does not carry, so it is the only one of the three that is not a pure CSS swap.
